Stylometry for fact-checking and monitoring

Find publications written from the same template

DIMS compares the writing style of texts from different channels and sites and flags pairs that are too similar to be independent. You get an integrated risk score with an explanation for every indicator.

Get early access How it works

The first 100 users get Pro for $9 a year.

A coordinated campaign gives itself away through style, not topic

When several channels post the same text with minor edits, checking each post separately takes hours. A shared topic proves nothing on its own: everyone writes about the same event.

Stylometry compares the frequencies of the most common words. This fingerprint barely depends on the topic and survives reordering and word swaps, so a shared template or a shared author shows up within seconds.

Three steps from sources to report

  1. 01

    Add sources

    TXT, PDF, DOCX, RTF and HTML files, article links or pasted text. Or collect material through Google News, RSS feeds and public Telegram channels.

  2. 02

    Run the analysis

    DIMS computes the Burrows' Delta distance for every pair of texts, builds a dendrogram, a heatmap and a projection of sources, and flags pairs below the θΔ threshold.

  3. 03

    Get the report

    An integrated RDIMS score, a grade from F to SSS, confidence intervals for every pair and a report ready to print or save as PDF.

One score, five explainable indicators

Stylometric similarity is only one signal. DIMS weighs five indicators and shows the contribution of each, so the analyst can see where the score comes from.

RDIMS= w1·Icontent+w2·Icoord+w3·Idynamics+w4·Iimpact+w5·Isource
  • Icontent

    Content

    Manipulative markers, emotional vocabulary, tone.

  • Icoord

    Coordination

    Stylometric similarity and synchronised publishing.

  • Idynamics

    Dynamics

    Spread rate and timing patterns.

  • Iimpact

    Impact

    Reach and replication of the material.

  • Isource

    Source

    Domain, owner, signs of editorial policy.

Grade scale

  1. FLow interest
  2. BLimited interest
  3. SClear interest
  4. SSSignificant interest
  5. SSSCritical interest

Limits of the method

Scientific basis

The method builds on Burrows' Delta and was developed as part of doctoral research in information systems and technologies.

Burrows, J. (2002). ‘Delta’: a Measure of Stylistic Difference and a Guide to Likely Authorship. Literary and Linguistic Computing, 17(3), 267–287.

  • Stylometric similarity is an indicator, not proof. A low Δ can mean a shared author, a shared template or simply the same genre. In the demo set, two independent news reports also scored Δ = 0.44.
  • Reliable results need texts of 500 words or more. DIMS flags shorter ones with a warning.
  • All-word analysis works with any language. Function-word mode currently supports Ukrainian, Russian and English.
  • A person decides whether something is disinformation, after checking the facts and the context.

FAQ

Does DIMS prove that a text is disinformation?

No. DIMS shows stylistic similarity and an overall risk level. A person draws the conclusion after checking the facts and the context.

Which text languages are supported?

All-word analysis works with any language that separates words with spaces. Function-word mode currently supports Ukrainian, Russian and English. Compare texts written in the same language.

What language is the interface in?

Ukrainian for now. An English interface is planned.

What happens to my texts?

Texts are used only for analysis in your account and are not shared with third parties.

How do I pay and cancel?

By Visa or Mastercard, Apple Pay or Google Pay. You can cancel at any time and keep access until the end of the paid period.

Can DIMS run on our own server?

Yes. The Team plan includes deployment on your infrastructure.
